decisions.question: MB-85 TKT-1 ticket header (text home Spec 08 §11.9): M-501
decisions.recommendation: CARD ~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/MB-85/CARD-ticket-status.md. Rule text: Ticket header. The first lines of every brief and prompt (after any front-matter block) are: `Ticket: MB-nn · lane X · stage N` (queue Process 11); `Rule:` the rule quoted with file:line; `Scope:` the files or targets; `Done-condition:`; `max_fix_rounds:` a number; when the header omits it the default is 2 (D6 B). Wider scope than the header is a new MB item, not a longer brief. every brief also opens its body, directly after the front-matter block, with the ticket header of §11.9 (TKT-1). The engine ignores any front-matter key it does not parse (`scripts/lib/exec-brief.js:20`), so the header sits in the body: no code change, and `write_scope` parsing is untouched. every brief and prompt, for every seat and lane agent (Claude and DeepSeek), opens with the ticket header, `Ticket: MB-nn · lane X · stage N`, the rule quoted with file:line, scope, done-condition and `max_fix_rounds`; every lane report and seat reply ends with one line `STATUS: ready\|blocked\|failed\|dropped` and at most one question. A reply-level word: it never changes a queue status cell (Status words below stay as they are). Rule text: Spec 08 §11.9 (TKT-1..TKT-4).
decisions.operator_quote: push complete - let's take the 1-4 as you suggested can will also apply any learnings ie status to the non deepseek part of our queue system as well.

decisions.question: MB-85 TKT-2 closed reply status (text home Spec 08 §11.9, §10.1): M-502
decisions.recommendation: CARD ~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/MB-85/CARD-ticket-status.md. Rule text: Closed reply status. Every reply ends with one line `STATUS: ready\|blocked\|failed\|dropped` and carries at most one question. ready: the done-condition is met and the evidence is in the reply. blocked: a ruling, card or input is missing; the question names it. failed: the work did not complete, or the reply is empty or truncated (TKT-4). dropped: the ticket is withdrawn or superseded; the reason is one line. This is a reply-level word. It never writes a queue status cell: the queue's own words (DONE, RUNNING, WAITS, OPERATOR, HELD, LATER; stage 10 is set by the checker) stay as they are. the TICKET and CLOSE lines of §10.1 apply to every seat in §10.2, Claude and DeepSeek alike (§11.9); a CLI or DeepSeek prompt carries the same two lines. every brief and prompt, for every seat and lane agent (Claude and DeepSeek), opens with the ticket header, `Ticket: MB-nn · lane X · stage N`, the rule quoted with file:line, scope, done-condition and `max_fix_rounds`; every lane report and seat reply ends with one line `STATUS: ready\|blocked\|failed\|dropped` and at most one question. A reply-level word: it never changes a queue status cell (Status words below stay as they are). Rule text: Spec 08 §11.9 (TKT-1..TKT-4).
decisions.operator_quote: push complete - let's take the 1-4 as you suggested can will also apply any learnings ie status to the non deepseek part of our queue system as well.

decisions.question: MB-85 TKT-3 McProof answer-first (text home Spec 08 §11.9 (§11.7 note)): M-503
decisions.recommendation: CARD ~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/MB-85/CARD-ticket-status.md. Rule text: McProof answer-first. A McProof reply puts its answers first, in the answer table the code already requires (`scripts/analysis/mcproof/prompts.mjs:10`, one row per example id: a number with an optional unit, a closed status, or `cannot decide`); the working follows the table. Rows outside the table are not read. MCPROOF-3 and MCPROOF-13 gain the answer-first and empty-or-truncated rules of §11.9 (TKT-3, TKT-4). The text above stands.
decisions.operator_quote: push complete - let's take the 1-4 as you suggested can will also apply any learnings ie status to the non deepseek part of our queue system as well.

decisions.question: MB-85 TKT-4 empty or truncated is failed (text home Spec 08 §11.9, §9): M-504
decisions.recommendation: CARD ~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/MB-85/CARD-ticket-status.md. Rule text: Empty or truncated is failed. An empty or truncated reply is `failed`, never a verdict and never a pass. One concise rerun is allowed; a second empty or truncated reply parks the ticket with an operator card (MCPROOF-13). McProof stage runs keep the configured retry count (`scripts/analysis/mcproof/mcproof.config.json:69`, `max_retries_per_stage` = 2) until that value is moved by a ruling (OWED, infra, frozen): this rule changes no config and no code. Output-cap and stop-reason logging are infra and frozen. A truncated or empty reply that reads like a verdict (MB-85, 2026-11-06). A seat reply cut off by an output cap, or empty, can look like a pass because nothing in it objects. It is not a verdict: it is `failed` (§11.9 TKT-4). The cap and stop-reason logging live in the ask tool, which is not in this repo, and are infra, frozen, not part of this rule. MCPROOF-3 and MCPROOF-13 gain the answer-first and empty-or-truncated rules of §11.9 (TKT-3, TKT-4). The text above stands.

decisions.question: MB-85 BOARD-1 one open-work list (text home Queue lane board (dated note)): M-507
decisions.recommendation: CARD ~/Buildo-scratch/mcbylaws/MB-85/CARD-ticket-status.md. Rule text: One open-work list: this lane board. Each open row carries one waiting word (OPERATOR, WAITS or HELD), names its card, and carries an opened date and an expiry date 7 days later. At expiry it is resurfaced in the next decision list; it is never closed automatically. The status file is an index of MB-nn and MF-nn rows with the waiting word, card and date; it holds no state of its own, and "row owed" marks a row not yet in the queue until the next queue dated note. No tool and no code. One-time sweep (E5): a read-only lane lists the unanswered CARD files against their queue rows (answered elsewhere, open with a row, or open with no row); nothing is deleted.
